title: Celiac disease blood test
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It looks for antibodies that appear when the gut does not handle gluten well.
why: For frequent diarrhea, bloating, weight loss, anemia, slow growth in children, or if relatives have celiac disease.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: If you have already cut out bread and other foods with gluten
What medicines you take, especially steroids
If any relatives have celiac disease

prepare.title: Gluten
prepare.text: Most important: keep eating bread, pasta, and other wheat foods until the test. Without gluten, the test can look falsely normal.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: It is usually best in the morning before eating. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Do not start a gluten-free diet until you talk to your doctor
Results usually come in a few days. The lab will tell you when

faq.q: Can I cut out gluten before the test?
faq.a: No. You need to eat it as usual. Otherwise the test may show nothing.

faq.q: What happens if the test is positive?
faq.a: Usually the doctor sends you for an upper endoscopy with a biopsy to confirm it.

reminders.text: Celiac test tomorrow. Eat as usual and do not cut out gluten. Best to come before eating.
